top_story.headline: Rep. Jamie Raskin bill would put Trump-era "authoritarianism" in a permanent Smithsonian exhibit
top_story.dek: The House met for two minutes with no votes, but 22 measures were introduced.
paragraphs: On a day when the House met for two minutes and held no votes, Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-MD-8) introduced H.R. 10765, which would direct the Secretary of the Smithsonian Institution to collect, preserve and display, in a permanent exhibition at the National Museum of American History, artifacts reflecting "the rise of governmental propaganda, corruption, and authoritarianism" during the two presidencies of Donald J. Trump.

The bill text defines the periods as January 20, 2017 through January 20, 2021, and January 20, 2025 through January 20, 2029. It was referred to the Committee on House Administration and, for a period to be determined, the Committee on Natural Resources. The record lists no cosponsors at introduction.
Also introduced: H.Res. 1618 by Rep. Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ-5), marking the third anniversary of the October 7, 2023, attacks on Israel, with more than 40 bipartisan cosponsors listed.

sections.headline: Pro forma sessions in both chambers; House introduces 22 measures
paragraphs: The Senate met in pro forma session for 33 seconds (1:31:12 p.m. to 1:31:45 p.m.) and adjourned until 1:30 p.m. on Friday, October 9, 2026. The House met at 4 p.m. and adjourned at 4:02 p.m. with no yea-and-nay votes, no recorded votes and no quorum calls.

The House Daily Digest counts 17 public bills (H.R. 10751-10767) and 5 resolutions (H.Con.Res. 123 and H.Res. 1617-1620). Two committee reports were also filed: H.R. 6698 (Board of Veterans' Appeals annual report on untimely appeals, H. Rept. 119-840) and H.R. 7260 (annual National Cemetery Administration report, H. Rept. 119-841). Most introductions are routine; all are listed below.

items: H.R. 10751, sponsored by Rep. Jack Bergman (R-MI-1) — Would remove restrictions on dental therapist services under the Community Health Aide Program of the Indian Health Care Improvement Act. Referred to the Committee on Natural Resources and the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10752, sponsored by Rep. Troy A. Carter (D-LA-2) — Would create a task force on artificial intelligence inside the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency. Referred to the Committee on Homeland Security.

H.R. 10753, sponsored by Rep. Elijah Crane (R-AZ-2) — Would direct the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development to set up a voluntary program to reallocate vouchers under the Tribal HUD-VASH program. Referred to the Committee on Financial Services.

H.R. 10754, sponsored by Rep. Elijah Crane (R-AZ-2) — Would update indicators of the local impact of a disaster in the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2018. Referred to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure.

H.R. 10755, sponsored by Rep. Jasmine Crockett (D-TX-30) — Would name the Cedar Hill, Texas, post office at 475 East FM 1382 the "Eugene Gates Jr. Post Office Building." Referred to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
H.R. 10756, sponsored by Rep. Mike Ezell (R-MS-4) — Would reauthorize Regional Ocean Partnerships. Referred to the Committee on Natural Resources.
H.R. 10757, sponsored by Rep. Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ-5) — Would limit United States contributions to the United Nations. Referred to the Committee on Foreign Affairs.

H.R. 10758, sponsored by Rep. Jeff Hurd (R-CO-3) — Would have the Secretary of Veterans Affairs award grants to state entities to expand structured outdoor recreation programs for veterans. Referred to the Committee on Veterans' Affairs.

H.R. 10759, sponsored by Rep. John James (R-MI-10) — Would create a tariff-funded program to shield United States manufacturers, workers, farmers and supply chains from economic harm caused by tariffs and foreign retaliation, and to encourage reshoring. Referred to the Committee on Financial Services and the Committee on Ways and Means.

H.R. 10760, sponsored by Rep. Thomas H. Kean (R-NJ-7) — Would create a multiagency Middle School Mental Health Task Force at the Department of Education and the Department of Health and Human Services. Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce and the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10761, sponsored by Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA-17) — Would amend the Jeanne Clery Campus Safety Act to combat campus sexual assault. Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce and the Committee on the Judiciary.

H.R. 10762, sponsored by Rep. Michael Lawler (R-NY-17) — Would require sellers of used motor vehicles to maintain a functional airbag system or clearly disclose when any airbag system is missing or disabled. Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce and the Committee on the Judiciary.

H.R. 10763, sponsored by Rep. Julia Letlow (R-LA-5) — (the Know Your Risk Act) would direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services to report to Congress on breast cancer risk assessment tools. Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10764, sponsored by Rep. Gwen Moore (D-WI-4) — Would require certain procedures for compromise settlements or awards involving executive branch officials. Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

H.R. 10765, sponsored by Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-MD-8) — Would direct the Secretary of the Smithsonian Institution to collect, preserve and display in a permanent National Museum of American History exhibition artifacts reflecting the rise of governmental propaganda, corruption and authoritarianism during the two presidencies of Donald J. Trump. Referred to the Committee on House Administration and the Committee on Natural Resources.

H.R. 10766, sponsored by Rep. Keith Self (R-TX-3) — Would direct the Secretary of Defense to add assets critical to the Golden Dome missile defense system to the Department of Defense Critical Asset List. Referred to the Committee on Armed Services.

H.R. 10767, sponsored by Rep. Adrian Smith (R-NE-3) — Would impose an excise tax on colleges and universities that allow specified individuals to take part in intercollegiate athletics. Referred to the Committee on Ways and Means.

H.Con.Res. 123, sponsored by Rep. Teresa Leger Fernandez (D-NM-3) — Would recognize the disparity in wages paid to Latinas and its impact on women, families and the economy; it has 22 listed cosponsors. Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce.
H.Res. 1617, sponsored by Rep. Earl L. "Buddy" Carter (R-GA-1) — Would recognize October as "American Pharmacy Month." Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.Res. 1618, sponsored by Rep. Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ-5) — Would mark the third anniversary of the October 7, 2023, attacks on Israel, honor the victims and hostages, and call for the complete disarmament of Hamas; it lists more than 40 cosponsors. Referred to the Committee on Foreign Affairs.

H.Res. 1619, sponsored by Rep. Glenn Thompson (R-PA-15) — Would reaffirm German-American friendship and support continued cooperation between the United States and Germany. Referred to the Committee on Foreign Affairs.

H.Res. 1620, sponsored by Rep. Nikema Williams (D-GA-5) — Would support the goals of "National Nonviolence Week" to raise awareness of youth violence. Referred to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
